t: G35 Cinematic Engine: Frame Budget Desk — Simple
name: G35 Cinematic Engine: Frame Budget Desk — Simple
title: G35 Cinematic Engine: Frame Budget Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Cinema runs at 24 frames per second: each frame gets 41.67 ms, and a 2-hour feature is 172,800 frames. The desk computes the frame count and the per-frame time budget — the numbers that size the render farm and the edit schedule.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Frame interval at 24 fps = 41.6667 ms. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: 24 fps frame math is the real, universal basis of cinema.
signature_version: Signature version: the NCC frame desk — the chapter's Narrative Coherence Constant as the pacing target, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: lock the frame rate before budgeting anything else.
math_note: Frame interval at 24 fps: 41.6667 ms [verified]; Frames in a 90-minute feature: 129600 frames [verified]
safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a schedule built on the wrong frame count.

The desk computes the code-value budget per stop — 10 bits gives 1024 steps, and the pipeline allocates them where the eye sees banding first.
